prisoner.name: Mary Tremblay
prisoner.description: Mary Tremblay was a member of Appeal to Reason who opposed the Seabrook nuclear power project in New Hampshire. After an initial February 22, 1982 leafletting protest and suspended sentence, the two returned to Public Service Company offices on February 26 and were jailed. They pleaded guilty and received six-month sentences. A contemporary follow-up confirms release on June 26, 1982 after four months in custody.
prisoner.body: Sources: April15,1982 newsletter page1; Follow-up, printedpage8/PDF10. The initial February22 episode is not counted as continuous custody through the second arrest.

case.charges: Civil-disobedience leafletting inside Public Service Company offices opposing Seabrook; exact statutory count unverified.
case.sentence: Six-month sentence following February26,1982 re-arrest; actually held until June26,1982. Mary at Rockingham County jail; David at Hillsborough County jail. Earlier February22 arrest ended in a suspended sentence and release, not continuous custody.

prisoner.name: Larry Moreland
prisoner.description: Larry Moreland was imprisoned after an antiwar protest that marked the Pentagon with Reagan-Herod graffiti during the December 1983 Feast of the Innocents actions. The March28,1984 Nuclear Resister reports that he was found guilty in mid-February, sentenced to one year with six months suspended, and was serving the remaining six months at Petersburg Farm Camp in Virginia. His exact admission and release dates remain unverified.
prisoner.body: Source: Nuclear Resister24, March28,1984, printedpage5/PDF6. Historical imprisonment is documented; present custody is not claimed.

case.charges: Pentagon antiwar graffiti protest; exact statutory count unverified.
case.sentence: One year, six months suspended; actual confinement at Petersburg Farm Camp reported March28,1984. February1984 sentencing is recorded at month precision, not February1 as an exact day. Actual total served and exact admission/release days unverified.
